reason: Refuted under the value lens. Transfer is fine: it is runtime only, public and private come from one run, it has no learned part and no node-count effect, and it is not a closed line. But the gain is ~1e-5, and it cannot be seen on a 3-decimal LB. (1) The why_now premise is wrong twice. (a) The 0.2 h margin is measured against an UPPER bound: K2 <= ~7.8 h comes from L35 <= 7.73 h, and that latency includes queue time. The true margin is probably larger. (b) 'Riders go after the insertion, so they cannot delay its gate' is false. Clips repair one after another (step0.md), so a rider on clip i delays the gate check (tools/build_probe_kernel.py l.1396-1402) on clip i+1. That point is moot anyway: forkmid is a last graph edit costing ~0 s/clip and the K3b DeepCenter threshold costs 0 s. So no planned rider has a runtime cost that the move would absorb. The '< 7 s/clip' rider rule it wants to relax is not in CONTEXT or FINAL_REPORT, and no planned rider falls in the 7-40 s/clip band. (2) Recomputed from the metric. The insertion is worth ~+0.001 per unit clip fraction (#35-#34, rounded LB). Full vs degraded repair is ~0.010 per unit fraction (gap/readmit/relink; safetail keeps safe divisions and linefit). Model: N=97, r0 61 s + 66 s insertion, anchor 7.79 h, uniform slowdown s. L2 (32400/37800) minus current (28800/34200) is +1e-5 at s=1.03, +5e-5 at 1.05, +1.5e-4 at 1.10 and +2.1..2.5e-4 at s=1.15-1.40. So the DIVINS move is worth at most a quarter of the insertion's own ~0.001. At s=1.5 the +1.2e-3 comes from the REPAIR raise (REPAIR-only gives +1.0e-3), which the h1 verdict already judged. At s >= 1.6 the REPAIR-only variant BEATS L2: the extra insertion hour pushes clips into the degraded path, and those are worth ~10x more per clip. P(s >= 1.05 against an upper-bound anchor, same code and same hidden hardware) ~0.05-0.15 (a guess). So E ~1e-5 to 2e-5, not the claimed ~1e-4. (3) Downside: at s=2 with the worst degraded clip (45.7 s), L2 ends at 11.75 h vs 10.67 h today, against a 12 h clock that starts before KERNEL_START_TS. The timeout cliff moves closer (visible as an error, not a silent private loss). (4) The proposed gate (sha256 of the K3 dummy with and without the change) only proves 'no effect' and can never certify a gain. It costs ~0.3 GPU-h from the 11 h quota shared with the exp60 lab. (5) The builder claim is partly wrong: DIVINS_DEADLINE_S is not whitelisted (l.1855 only needs --patch safetail). Only REPAIR_DEADLINE_S is pinned to 34200 (l.1849).
fix: Do not adopt as a default for K3/K3b/F1-final. Keep DIVINS_DEADLINE_S=28800 and REPAIR_DEADLINE_S=34200. Pre-register a trigger instead. Raise DIVINS by +1 h (to 32400) only if (a) the observed L(K2) > 8.0 h, or (b) a rider's dummy (e.g. tempfuse in the GPU phase) adds > ~7 s/clip x N~97 before the last clip's gate. Raise it only TOGETHER with REPAIR_DEADLINE_S +1 h (37800, which needs the builder whitelist and test_safetail case from the h1 fix), so the gap between the two gates stays >= 1.5 h. Never move DIVINS alone. Before activating, check that 10.5 h + N x 45.7 s x s_forecast <= 11.5 h. Drop the sha-twin dummy. Record per-rider dummy s/clip in the runtime ledger proposed in the h1 value verdict.
realistic_gain: ~+1e-5 to +2e-5 expected (public = private, one run). It is exactly 0 in every world where the hidden run is < ~1.03x the upper-bound anchor, which includes all observed runs (L34 <= 6.46 h, L35 <= 7.73 h). The cap is ~+2.5e-4 even at a 1.15-1.4x slowdown. It turns negative against a REPAIR-only raise at >= 1.6x. Cost is ~0 for the knob, plus ~0.3 GPU-h if the proposed sha-twin dummy is run.
